paragraph: In 2025, [exports of information and communication technology (ICT) services from Angola were 0.0168 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP)](<https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/BX.GSR.CCIS.CD>), by the World Bank's series of computer and telecom services sold abroad. The same series [put the share at 0.0406 per cent in 2021 and 0.0279 per cent in 2024](<https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/BX.GSR.CCIS.CD>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No plant making ICT equipment in the country has been found. Preparing would need ICT service exports of 0.05 per cent of GDP or more in the latest figure, for 2023 or later.

[TECOO, a Burundian company at Buringa in Bujumbura Rural, assembles small mobile phones](<https://andikamagazine.net/burundis-tecoo-expands-local-tech-manufacturing-aims-for-smartphones-and-batteries/>). Its founder told Andika Magazine in December 2025 that it employs more than 70 workers. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need ICT service exports of 0.2 per cent of GDP or more, and the latest figure is below that.

[Horizon Industries, at Kossodo in Ouagadougou, assembles laptops, phones, tablets and household appliances](<https://digitalmagazine.bf/2025/02/23/burkina-faso-un-accord-historique-pour-la-production-locale-dequipements-informatiques-avec-horizon-industries-la-premiere-unite-de-montage-dequipements-electroniques-au-burkina/>). The state holds 35% of it through FBDES. [In December 2025 Sciences Check confirmed it is an assembly plant](<https://sciencescheck.org/faux-cette-usine-ne-fabrique-pas-des-ordinateurs-portables-au-burkina-faso/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No plant making ICT equipment in the country has been found. Operating would need ICT service exports of 0.5 per cent of GDP or more.

In 2024, [exports of information and communication technology (ICT) services from Tanzania were 0.0867 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP)](<https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/BX.GSR.CCIS.CD>), by the World Bank's series of computer and telecommunications services sold abroad. [TanzTech Electronics in Arusha has assembled smartphones, tablets, laptops and projectors since 2023](<https://dailynews.co.tz/arusha-electronics-firm-to-boost-local-tech-industry/>). In 2024, [ICT service exports from Uganda were 0.0899 per cent of GDP](<https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/BX.GSR.CCIS.CD>), by the World Bank's series of computer and telecommunications services sold abroad. It works from the Kampala Industrial and Business Park at Namanve. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need ICT service exports of 0.2 per cent of GDP or more.
